question.text: A function $\mathrm{f}$ from the set of natural numbers to integers defined by $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{n})=\left\{\begin{array}{l}\frac{\mathrm{n}-1}{2} \text {, when } n \text { isodd } \\ \frac{\mathrm{n}}{2} \text {, when } \mathrm{n} \text { is even }\end{array}\right.$ is

solution.text:
$f: N \rightarrow 1$ $f(1)=0, f(2)=-1, f(3)=-1, f(4)=-2$ $f(5)=2$, and $f(6)=-3$ so on.
In this type of function every element of set $\mathrm{A}$ has unique image in set $\mathrm{B}$ and there is no element left in set $\mathrm{B}$. Hence $\mathrm{f}$ is one-one and onto function.
